title: Bakery-Style Blueberry Muffins
description: Tall, domed muffins with a tender buttermilk crumb, a berry in every bite, and a crackly sugar top. A hot start in the oven gives them their bakery height.
notes: The oven starts at 425°F and is turned down to 375°F after 7 minutes; the first blast of heat sets the tall dome. Have the buttermilk and eggs at room temperature so the melted butter does not seize into lumps. Frozen blueberries go in straight from the freezer; thawed berries streak the batter purple. No buttermilk: stir 1 tbsp lemon juice into 1 cup whole milk and let it stand 5 minutes. Store airtight at room temperature for 2 days with a paper towel under the lid, or freeze for up to 3 months and rewarm at 300°F for 10 minutes.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter, melted and cooled slightly (113 g)
blueberries, fresh or frozen and not thawed (300 g)
turbinado or granulated sugar, for the tops

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the center. Line a 12-cup standard muffin tin with paper liners and lightly grease the flat top of the pan so the muffin crowns release.
In a large bowl, whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt for 30 seconds so the leavening is evenly spread.
In a medium bowl, whisk the melted butter and granulated sugar until combined, then whisk in the eggs one at a time. Whisk in the buttermilk, vanilla, and lemon zest until the mixture is smooth.

Pour the wet ingredients over the dry and fold with a spatula until only a few streaks of flour remain. Add the blueberries and fold just until they are distributed and no dry flour shows. The batter will be thick and lumpy; do not beat it smooth.
Divide the batter among the 12 cups, mounding it right to the top of each liner (a heaping 1/3 cup each). Sprinkle the tops with the turbinado sugar.

Bake at 425°F for 7 minutes. Without opening the door, lower the oven to 375°F and bake 15 to 18 minutes more, until the muffins are domed and golden, the tops spring back when pressed, and a toothpick in the center comes out with no wet batter (a blueberry stain is fine).
Cool the muffins in the pan for 5 minutes, then move them to a wire rack so the bottoms do not steam. Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Soft Cinnamon Rolls with Cream Cheese Glaze
description: Pillowy yeasted rolls wrapped around a brown sugar and cinnamon swirl, finished warm with a tangy cream cheese glaze that melts into every layer.
equipment: stand mixer with dough hook or large bowl
notes: Plan on about 2 hours of rising in addition to the prep and bake times: 1 to 1 1/2 hours for the first rise and 30 to 45 minutes for the second. Go by the look of the dough, not the clock; a cool kitchen takes longer. Milk hotter than 115°F can kill the yeast. Overnight option: after shaping, cover the pan tightly and refrigerate up to 16 hours, then let the rolls stand at room temperature until puffy, 45 to 60 minutes, before baking. Unflavored dental floss slid under the log and crossed over the top cuts cleaner rolls than a knife. Because of the cream cheese glaze, refrigerate leftovers after a few hours; keep covered for up to 4 days and rewarm single rolls for 20 seconds in the microwave. Unglazed baked rolls freeze well for 2 months.

ingredients.name: whole milk, warmed to 100 to 110°F (240 ml)
instant or active dry yeast (1 packet, 7 g)
unsalted butter, melted and cooled slightly (76 g)
all-purpose flour (530 g), plus more for dusting
whole milk, plus more as needed to thin the glaze

instructions: In the bowl of a stand mixer or a large bowl, stir the warm milk (100 to 110°F, comfortably warm on your wrist), the yeast, and 1 tablespoon of the granulated sugar. Let stand 5 minutes until the surface looks foamy.

Whisk in the remaining granulated sugar, the eggs, and the melted butter. Add the flour and salt and mix until a shaggy dough forms. Knead with the dough hook on medium-low for 6 to 8 minutes, or by hand on a lightly floured counter for 8 to 10 minutes, until the dough is smooth, elastic, and slightly tacky but no longer sticks to your fingers. Add flour 1 tablespoon at a time only if it stays sticky.

Shape the dough into a ball, place it in a lightly greased bowl, cover, and let it rise in a warm spot until doubled in size, 1 to 1 1/2 hours. A floured fingertip pressed into the dough should leave a dent that fills back slowly.

Grease a 9x13-inch baking pan. Stir the brown sugar and cinnamon together. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and roll it into an 18x12-inch rectangle with a long side facing you. Spread the very soft butter over the dough to the edges, then sprinkle the cinnamon sugar evenly over it and press it in lightly.

Starting from the long side nearest you, roll the dough up into a snug log and pinch the seam closed. Cut the log into 12 equal rolls, each about 1 1/2 inches wide, and arrange them cut side up in the pan in 3 rows of 4.
Cover the pan and let the rolls rise until puffy and touching one another, 30 to 45 minutes. Meanwhile, heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the center.

Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until the rolls are golden brown on top and the center roll reads 190°F on an instant-read thermometer. If the tops brown early, lay a sheet of foil loosely over the pan for the last 10 minutes.

While the rolls bake, beat the cream cheese and softened butter until completely smooth, then beat in the powdered sugar, vanilla, and 1 tablespoon milk until creamy and spreadable, adding a little more milk if it is too thick.
Let the rolls cool for 10 minutes, then spread the glaze over them while they are still warm so it sinks into the swirls. Serve warm.

title: No-Water-Bath New York-Style Cheesecake
description: A tall, dense, creamy cheesecake on a buttery graham cracker crust, baked gently and cooled slowly in the oven so it stays smooth without the fuss of a water bath.
notes: Start a day ahead: after baking, the cheesecake rests 1 hour in the turned-off oven, cools 1 to 2 hours at room temperature, then chills at least 6 hours, ideally overnight, before slicing. Every cold ingredient should be at true room temperature (set them out 2 hours ahead) or the batter will be lumpy. Mix on low speed; whipping in air makes the cake puff, then sink and crack. Do not open the oven during the first 50 minutes. The cheesecake is done when the outer 2 to 3 inches look set and slightly puffed and the center still wobbles like set gelatin, about 150°F in the middle; it finishes setting as it cools. For clean slices, dip a long knife in hot water and wipe it between cuts. Keeps covered in the refrigerator for 5 days, or freeze without toppings, well wrapped, for up to 2 months and thaw overnight in the refrigerator.

ingredients.name: graham cracker crumbs (150 g, from about 10 full sheets)
full-fat brick cream cheese (four 8-oz blocks), at room temperature
full-fat sour cream, at room temperature (240 g)

instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F with a rack in the center. Lightly grease the sides of a 9-inch springform pan and line the bottom with a round of parchment.

Stir the graham cracker crumbs, 2 tablespoons sugar, melted butter, and pinch of salt until the mixture looks like damp sand and holds together when squeezed. Press it firmly and evenly over the bottom of the pan and about 1/2 inch up the sides, using the flat bottom of a measuring cup. Bake for 10 minutes, until fragrant and a shade darker, then set aside to cool while you make the filling. Leave the oven on.

In a large bowl, beat the cream cheese on low speed for 1 to 2 minutes, scraping the bowl and beater twice, until completely smooth with no lumps. Mix the 1 1/4 cups sugar, cornstarch, and 1/4 teaspoon salt together, add them to the cream cheese, and beat on low just until blended.

Add the sour cream, lemon juice, and vanilla and mix on low until smooth, scraping the bowl well. Add the eggs one at a time, mixing on low only until each one disappears into the batter. Stop as soon as the last egg is blended in.
Pour the filling over the crust and smooth the top. Tap the pan firmly on the counter 5 or 6 times to bring air bubbles to the surface, then set it on a rimmed baking sheet.

Bake at 325°F for 60 to 70 minutes without opening the oven for the first 50. The cheesecake is ready when the outer 2 to 3 inches are set and slightly puffed and the center 3 inches still jiggle as one piece, like set gelatin, when you nudge the pan (about 150°F in the center). It should not ripple like liquid.
Turn the oven off, prop the door open about 1 inch with a wooden spoon, and leave the cheesecake inside for 1 hour. This slow cool-down is what prevents cracks.
Move the pan to a wire rack and run a thin knife around the edge to release the cake from the sides so it can shrink without tearing. Cool to room temperature, 1 to 2 hours.

Cover the pan loosely and refrigerate for at least 6 hours or overnight, until cold and firm all the way through. Release the springform ring, slice with a hot, clean knife, and serve plain or with fresh berries.

title: Classic Lemon Bars with Shortbread Crust
description: A crisp, buttery press-in shortbread base under a bright, sharply lemony filling that bakes until fully set. They slice cleanly once chilled and need nothing but a dusting of powdered sugar.
notes: Use freshly squeezed lemon juice; bottled juice tastes flat here. You will need 3 to 4 lemons, and it is easiest to zest them before juicing. Line the pan with parchment rather than baking directly in bare aluminum, which can give the acidic filling a metallic taste. The filling goes onto the crust while the crust is still hot so the two layers bond and the base stays crisp. Bake until the center no longer jiggles when the pan is nudged (at least 170°F), so the eggs are fully cooked. Cool 1 hour at room temperature, then chill at least 2 hours before cutting. A thin, pale, crackly film on top is just air from whisking and is hidden by the powdered sugar; dust right before serving because the sugar dissolves as it sits. Refrigerate, covered, for up to 5 days, or freeze undusted bars for 2 months.

ingredients.name: fresh lemon juice, strained (120 ml, from 3 to 4 lemons)

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the center. Line an 8x8-inch metal baking pan with two crossed strips of parchment, leaving an overhang on all four sides to lift the bars out later.

In a medium bowl, stir the melted butter, 1/4 cup sugar, and 1/4 teaspoon salt together. Add the 1 1/4 cups flour and stir until a soft, thick dough forms with no dry flour left. Press it into the lined pan in an even layer, right into the corners.
Bake the crust for 18 to 20 minutes, until the surface looks dry and the edges are lightly golden.

While the crust bakes, whisk the 1 cup sugar, 3 tablespoons flour, and pinch of salt in a large bowl until no lumps of flour remain. Add the eggs and whisk gently until smooth, then whisk in the lemon zest and juice. Whisk only enough to combine so you do not beat in a lot of air.

As soon as the crust comes out, give the filling a quick stir and pour it over the hot crust. Return the pan to the oven and bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until the filling is set from edge to edge and the center does not jiggle or ripple when you gently nudge the pan.
Cool the pan on a wire rack for 1 hour, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours, until the filling is cold and firm.
Lift the slab out by the parchment, peel the paper away from the sides, and cut into 16 squares with a sharp knife, wiping the blade between cuts. Dust with the powdered sugar just before serving.

title: Rustic Apple Galette with All-Butter Crust
description: A free-form apple tart with a flaky, deeply browned all-butter crust folded over cinnamon-scented apples. It has all the pleasure of apple pie with no pie plate and no crimping.
notes: The dough needs at least 1 hour in the refrigerator before rolling (up to 2 days, or freeze for 2 months), and the shaped galette benefits from 15 minutes of chilling before it bakes; neither is included in the prep time. Keep the butter cold and visible in the dough: flat, pea-size pieces are what make flaky layers. Add only enough water for the dough to hold together when squeezed; extra water makes a tough crust. Use firm apples that hold their shape, such as Granny Smith, Honeycrisp, Pink Lady, or a mix. Bake on the lower-third rack and judge doneness by the bottom of the crust, which should be browned and crisp, not pale. Best the day it is baked; keep leftovers loosely covered at room temperature for 1 day or refrigerated for 4, and re-crisp at 350°F for 10 minutes.

ingredients.name: all-purpose flour (155 g), plus more for rolling
cold unsalted butter, cut into 1/2-inch cubes (113 g)
ice water, plus up to 2 tbsp more as needed
firm baking apples (3 large or 4 medium), peeled, cored, and sliced 1/4 inch thick
cold unsalted butter, cut into small bits (14 g)
large egg, beaten with 1 tsp water, for brushing
turbinado or granulated sugar, for sprinkling

instructions: Make the crust: whisk the flour, 1 tablespoon sugar, and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a large bowl. Add the cold butter cubes and rub them into the flour with your fingertips or a pastry blender until the largest pieces are the size of flattened peas and the rest looks like coarse meal.

Sprinkle 3 tablespoons ice water over the flour and toss with a fork. Add more water 1 teaspoon at a time, only until the dough holds together when you squeeze a handful and no dry flour remains at the bottom of the bowl. Press it into a 1-inch-thick disk, wrap tightly, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the lower third. In a large bowl, toss the sliced apples with 1/4 cup sugar, the cornstarch, cinnamon, lemon juice, and pinch of salt until evenly coated.

On a lightly floured sheet of parchment, roll the chilled dough into a 12-inch round about 1/8 inch thick; ragged edges are fine. If it cracks, let it sit 5 minutes to soften slightly. Slide the parchment and dough onto a rimmed baking sheet.

Arrange the apples over the dough in overlapping layers or an even mound, leaving a 2-inch border bare and leaving any pooled juices behind in the bowl. Dot the apples with the bits of butter. Fold the border up and over the edge of the fruit, pleating it every few inches and pressing the pleats gently to seal. Chill the galette on its pan for 15 minutes.
Brush the folded crust with the beaten egg and sprinkle the crust and apples with the turbinado sugar.

Bake for 40 to 50 minutes, rotating the pan once after 25 minutes, until the crust is deep golden brown, the juices are bubbling, the apples are tender when pierced with a knife, and the underside is browned when you lift an edge with a spatula.
Cool on the baking sheet for at least 20 minutes so the juices thicken, then slide the galette onto a board and cut into 8 wedges. Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Margherita Pizza with Homemade Dough
description: A simple, hand-kneaded dough baked hot into two crisp-edged, chewy pizzas topped with crushed tomatoes, fresh mozzarella, and basil. No mixer and no cooked sauce required.
equipment: baking steel, pizza stone, or heavy rimmed baking sheet
notes: Makes two 12-inch pizzas. The dough rises for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, which is not included in the prep time; for more flavor, let it rise 30 minutes at room temperature, then refrigerate it for 1 to 3 days and bring it back to room temperature for 1 hour before shaping. Bread flour gives a chewier crust, but all-purpose works in the same amount. Drain the tomatoes and pat the mozzarella dry, since extra moisture is the main cause of a soggy center. Most parchment is rated to about 450°F, so trim it close to the dough and slide it out from under the pizza after 4 minutes; a well-floured peel or the back of a baking sheet also works. If you do not eat animal rennet, check the mozzarella label. Leftover slices keep refrigerated for 3 days; reheat in a dry covered skillet over medium heat until the bottom crisps. Dough balls freeze for 2 months.

ingredients.name: bread flour or all-purpose flour (375 g), plus more for shaping
extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for the bowl
whole peeled tomatoes (14 to 15 oz), drained
fresh mozzarella, torn into 1-inch pieces and patted dry

instructions: In a large bowl, stir the flour, yeast, and 1 1/2 teaspoons salt together. Add the warm water (100 to 110°F) and 1 tablespoon olive oil and stir until a shaggy dough forms and no dry flour remains. Turn it out onto a lightly floured counter and knead for 6 to 8 minutes, until the dough is smooth, springy, and only slightly tacky.

Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, turn it to coat, and cover. Let it rise in a warm spot until doubled in size, 1 to 1 1/2 hours; a floured fingertip pressed in should leave a dent that springs back slowly.
At least 30 minutes before baking, set a baking steel, pizza stone, or upside-down heavy rimmed baking sheet on a rack in the upper third of the oven and heat the oven to 500°F.

Divide the dough into 2 equal pieces, shape each into a tight ball, cover, and let them rest for 15 minutes so they stretch easily. Meanwhile, crush the drained tomatoes with your hands or a fork into a chunky sauce and stir in 1/2 teaspoon salt and 1 tablespoon of the olive oil.

On a sheet of lightly floured parchment, press one ball of dough flat with your fingertips, then stretch it over your knuckles into a 12-inch round, leaving the outer 1/2 inch a little thicker. Trim the parchment to within 1 inch of the dough.
Spread half of the tomato sauce (about 1/3 cup) thinly over the dough, leaving the rim bare, and scatter half of the mozzarella over the top.

Slide the pizza on its parchment onto the hot steel, stone, or baking sheet. Bake for 8 to 10 minutes, pulling the parchment out after 4 minutes, until the rim is puffed and deeply browned in spots, the cheese is bubbling, and the underside is browned and crisp when you lift an edge.

Move the pizza to a cutting board, scatter with half of the basil, and drizzle with a little of the remaining olive oil. Let it rest for 2 minutes before slicing. Let the oven reheat for 5 minutes, then shape, top, and bake the second pizza the same way.

title: Overnight Baked French Toast Casserole
description: Cubes of challah soak overnight in a cinnamon-vanilla custard, then bake under a brown sugar streusel until puffed and golden with a soft, custardy center. All the work happens the night before.
notes: The assembled casserole needs at least 4 hours and up to 16 hours in the refrigerator so the bread soaks up the custard; that time is not included above. Slightly stale bread works best. If your loaf is fresh, spread the cubes on a baking sheet and dry them at 300°F for 10 to 15 minutes, then cool. Sturdy sandwich bread or French bread can stand in for the challah. If using a glass or ceramic dish, let it sit at room temperature while the oven heats so it does not go into the oven ice-cold. The casserole is done when the center is set with no liquid custard and reads at least 160°F. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and keep for up to 3 days; reheat covered at 325°F for 15 minutes. All milk can replace the cream for a lighter version.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter, softened, for the dish (14 g)
day-old challah or brioche bread, cut into 1-inch cubes (about 10 cups)
cold unsalted butter, cut into small cubes (57 g)
pure maple syrup, warmed, for serving

instructions: Rub the softened butter over the bottom and sides of a 9x13-inch baking dish. Spread the bread cubes in the dish in an even layer.
In a large bowl, whisk the eggs until no streaks of white remain. Whisk in the milk, cream, 1/3 cup brown sugar, vanilla, 1 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt until the sugar dissolves.
Pour the custard slowly and evenly over the bread, then press down gently with your hands so every cube is moistened. Cover the dish tightly and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.

Make the streusel: in a small bowl, mix the flour, 1/3 cup brown sugar, and 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon. Rub in the cold butter with your fingertips until the mixture forms damp clumps the size of peas. Cover and refrigerate until needed.
When ready to bake, heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the center and take the dish out of the refrigerator while the oven heats. Uncover it and scatter the streusel evenly over the top.

Bake uncovered for 45 to 55 minutes, until the casserole is puffed and golden brown, the streusel is crisp, and a knife slipped into the center comes out with no liquid custard (at least 160°F in the middle). If the top browns before the center sets, lay a sheet of foil loosely over the dish.
Let the casserole rest for 10 minutes so the custard firms up, then cut into squares and serve warm with the maple syrup.

title: Crunchy Maple Seed Granola
description: Golden, clumpy granola made with certified gluten-free oats, pumpkin and sunflower seeds, and maple syrup. It is vegan and nut-free, and it stays crisp for weeks.
notes: Makes about 5 1/2 cups; a serving is a generous 1/2 cup. For celiac-safe granola, the oats must be labeled certified gluten-free, and if you are baking for a nut allergy, check that the seeds and dried fruit are packed in a nut-free facility. The coconut is optional; leave it out for anyone who avoids coconut and add 1/4 cup more seeds instead. Use old-fashioned rolled oats, not quick or steel-cut. The granola still feels soft when it comes out of the oven and turns crunchy as it cools, so judge by color, not by touch. For big clusters, press it down before and during baking and let it cool completely, about 45 minutes, before breaking it up. Add dried fruit only after baking so it does not scorch. Store airtight at room temperature for 3 weeks or freeze for 3 months.

ingredients.name: certified gluten-free old-fashioned rolled oats (270 g)
extra-virgin olive oil or melted coconut oil (80 ml)
dried cranberries, raisins, or chopped dried apricots (70 g)

instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F with a rack in the center. Line an 18x13-inch rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, stir together the oats, pumpkin seeds, sunflower seeds, chia seeds, cinnamon, and salt.
Whisk the oil, maple syrup, and vanilla in a measuring cup until blended, pour over the oat mixture, and stir for a full minute, until every oat looks glossy and no dry patches remain.
Scrape the mixture onto the lined baking sheet, spread it into an even layer that reaches the corners, and press it down firmly with the back of a spatula.
Bake for 15 minutes. Take the pan out, sprinkle on the coconut flakes if using, and gently turn the granola in large sections, moving the darker edges toward the middle. Press it flat again.
Return the pan to the oven and bake 12 to 18 minutes more, until the granola is evenly deep golden and smells toasty. It will still feel slightly soft; it crisps as it cools.
Set the pan on a wire rack and let the granola cool completely without stirring, about 45 minutes. Break it into clusters, mix in the dried fruit, and transfer to an airtight container.

title: Strawberry-Banana Oat Breakfast Smoothie
description: A thick, creamy smoothie with enough staying power to count as breakfast, thanks to rolled oats, hemp hearts, and sunflower seed butter blended with frozen fruit.
notes: Makes two glasses of about 1 1/2 cups each. The oats, hemp hearts, and seed butter supply fiber, fat, and protein, so this holds you until lunch; a higher-protein plant milk such as pea milk adds more. Soy milk also works but adds soy as an allergen. Use oats labeled certified gluten-free for anyone with celiac disease, and check that the sunflower seed butter and plant milk come from a nut-free facility if you are serving someone with a nut allergy. Peel and slice ripe bananas before freezing them flat in a bag. If your fruit is fresh instead of frozen, add 1 cup of ice. Sunflower seed butter can turn a smoothie slightly green over time, which is harmless. Best right away; it keeps in a sealed jar in the refrigerator for 24 hours. Shake well before drinking.

ingredients.name: unsweetened nut-free plant milk, such as pea or gluten-free oat milk (360 ml), plus more to thin
certified gluten-free old-fashioned rolled oats (45 g)
large ripe banana, peeled, sliced, and frozen

instructions: Pour the plant milk into the blender, add the oats, and let them soak for 5 minutes so they soften and blend smoothly.
Blend the milk and oats on high for 30 seconds, until the oats are broken down and the liquid looks creamy with no visible flakes.
Add the frozen banana, frozen strawberries, hemp hearts, sunflower seed butter, vanilla, and salt to the blender.

Blend, starting on low and increasing to high, for 45 to 60 seconds, stopping once to scrape down the sides, until the smoothie is completely smooth, evenly pink, and thick enough to mound on a spoon.
Taste and blend in the maple syrup if you want it sweeter, or a splash more plant milk if it is too thick to pour. Divide between 2 glasses and serve right away.

title: Flaky Buttermilk Biscuits
description: Tall American-style biscuits with crisp golden tops and soft, buttery layers you can pull apart. Cold butter, cold buttermilk, and a few quick folds do all the work.
notes: Everything should be cold: cube the butter and return it to the refrigerator, and measure the buttermilk last. If the butter softens or smears while you work, chill the cut biscuits for 10 to 15 minutes before baking. Handle the dough as little as possible; a shaggy, slightly sticky dough makes tender biscuits. Cutting squares with a knife means no scraps to re-roll; if you use a round cutter, press straight down without twisting, which seals the edges and stops the rise. No buttermilk: stir 1 tbsp lemon juice or white vinegar into 1 cup whole milk and let it stand 5 minutes. Biscuits are best within a few hours. Store airtight for 2 days and rewarm at 350°F for 5 to 8 minutes, or freeze the unbaked cut biscuits and bake from frozen, adding 3 to 5 minutes.

ingredients.name: all-purpose flour (315 g), plus more for the counter
cold unsalted butter, cut into 1/2-inch cubes (113 g)
cold buttermilk (240 ml), plus 1 tbsp for brushing
unsalted butter, melted, for finishing (14 g)

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the upper-middle position. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt together for 30 seconds.

Add the cold butter cubes and toss to coat. Working quickly, press and rub the butter into the flour with your fingertips until the pieces range from pea-size bits to flat flakes the size of a nickel. Stop while the butter is still cold and clearly visible.
Pour in the cold buttermilk and stir with a fork just until a shaggy, slightly sticky dough forms and no dry flour sits at the bottom of the bowl, about 15 strokes.

Turn the dough onto a floured counter and pat it into a rectangle about 1 inch thick. Fold it in thirds like a letter, turn it a quarter turn, and pat it out again. Repeat the fold and turn 2 more times, dusting with flour only as needed, to build layers.

Pat the dough into a 5x8-inch rectangle about 1 inch thick. With a floured bench scraper or sharp knife, press straight down to cut it into 8 squares. Arrange them on the baking sheet about 1/2 inch apart so they support each other as they rise, and brush the tops with buttermilk.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until the biscuits have risen tall and the tops and bottoms are deep golden brown.
Brush the hot biscuits with the melted butter and let them cool on the pan for 5 minutes. Serve warm.
